decisions.reason: The source grants placement flexibility for connectors on the current integrated board but does not change the legacy interboard connector types, pinouts, roles, or power chain.
The candidate concerns connector accessibility and placement on the legacy power board; the source addresses general placement on the integrated board and does not revise those legacy constraints.
The source permits general connector placement but leaves the separately specified ESP32 antenna orientation and minimum keepout unchanged.
The candidate already specifies a single integrated board; the source relies on that topology but does not change it.
General connector-placement flexibility on the integrated board does not revise the legacy power-board dimensions, mounting, aspect ratio, or enclosure orientation.
Connector placement has no necessary effect on the legacy main board's four-layer requirement.
The source concerns connector-side placement on the integrated board and does not change the legacy main board's 70 by 50 millimeter dimensions.
The placement decision does not alter the integrated design's cost goal, component-selection policy, architecture, or elimination of interboard connectors.
General connector placement on the integrated board does not change the power board's layer count.
The source does not establish or revise any sensor-board layer-stack requirement.
The source changes where integrated-board connectors may be placed but does not change the sensor fanout's connector inventory, signals, role, or disabled interboard connectors.
Connector placement flexibility does not change whether legacy main-board BOM parts must resolve or whether the two adjacent connectors are optional to populate.
